D19·v6b3 — 2026-09-22
chose: Evaluator port isolation per cell, at the user's direction relayed by sofar-c3 on 2026-09-22. (1) Each evaluator cell, eval or fix, gets its own 10-port block, PORT = 10000 + (sha256("<run>/<arm>/r<rep>") mod 1000) × 10. It is exported to the agent the way round 2 exports its block (runner/lib/sandbox.ts cellPort), and the range 10000–19990 is disjoint from round 2's 20000–59990. (2) The candidate profile kernel-denies port 3000, the skeleton's hard-coded `next dev --port 3000`, for both binding and connecting: (deny network-bind (local ip "*:3000")) and (deny network-outbound (remote ip "localhost:3000")). An evaluator cell can then neither take a bench cell's default dev port nor talk to a bench cell's app there. Port-0 binds, other local ports and the internet stay open. (3) selfTest proves this before every launch: binding the cell port works, binding or connecting to :3000 is denied, and binding port 0 works. (4) The cycle wrapper drops its :3000 wait. It keeps the round-2 marker gate, because the user ruled that eval cells never run beside round 2's own runs; they share the $450 D17 week cap.
over: (a) Only exporting PORT, as round 2 does. The app's dev script ignores PORT, so an agent's `bun run dev` would still bind 3000 beside a bench cell. (b) An allowlist of the cell's 10 ports for all binds. It works, but it also denies port-0 binds, and `*:0` is invalid SBPL, so an agent's own tests that listen on a free port would fail. (c) Rewriting the cell's dev script to use $PORT, which changes the measured workload. (d) Denying round 2's whole block range, which SBPL cannot express as a range.
because: A tested Seatbelt profile (allow default plus the two :3000 denies) gives EPERM on bind and connect at :3000 over 127.0.0.1, ::, 0.0.0.0, ::1 and localhost, while port-0 binds, :3100 and 1.1.1.1:443 still work. The one collision the skeleton makes certain, two cells both on the hard-coded 3000, becomes impossible from the evaluator's side. An agent that picks another port explicitly is still advisory-only, as it is in round 2; that is the stated limit. The same profile applies to all three arms, so the comparison stays equal.
